info.title: Cella DEVELOPMENT API
info.description:
⚠️ ATTENTION: PRERELEASE!
                  This API is organized into modules based on logical domains.

x-extensions.description: Config switch the endpoint belongs to: a service, a sign-in method or an OAuth provider; refused before the guards while it is off
Authorization middleware applied to the endpoint

serviceGuard.name: service
serviceGuard.description: Requires a secret API key or an access token; acts as its service account or consenting user, limited to its scopes

userGuard.name: user
userGuard.description: Requires a session cookie; acts as the signed-in user

actorGuard.name: actor
actorGuard.description: Requires a session cookie, a secret API key or an access token; acts as the user or service account it proves

orgGuard.name: org
orgGuard.description: Requires being in the organization: a member of it or of a channel below it, or a system admin

relatableGuard.name: relatable
relatableGuard.description: Requires sharing an organization with the user the request names, or being a system admin

stepUpGuard.name: stepUp
stepUpGuard.description: Requires a recent proof of presence on this session: a passkey or TOTP the user holds, else a fresh sign-in or emailed link; refuses impersonation

sysAdminGuard.name: sysAdmin
sysAdminGuard.description: Requires the system admin role and an allowed IP address; refuses impersonation

tenantGuard.name: tenant
tenantGuard.description: Requires being in the tenant: a member, a system admin, or its creator while it has no organization

tokenGuard.name: token
tokenGuard.description: Requires an access token, no session or API key; acts as its service account or consenting user, limited to its scopes

x-extensions.description: Rate limiting rules applied to the endpoint

spamLimiter.name: spam
spamLimiter.description: Emails sent per user, per IP when anonymous: 10 per hour

emailEnumLimiter.name: emailEnum
emailEnumLimiter.description: Address lookups per IP, hits included: 30 per hour, then blocked for 30 minutes

presignedUrlLimiter.name: presignedUrl
presignedUrlLimiter.description: File links per user: 2000 per hour, then blocked for 15 minutes

totpVerificationLimiter.name: totpVerification
totpVerificationLimiter.description: Failed TOTP codes per IP: 5 per hour, then blocked for 30 minutes

stepUpLimiter.name: stepUp
stepUpLimiter.description: Failed step-up checks per account: 5 per hour, then blocked for 30 minutes

magicLinkLimiter.name: magicLink
magicLinkLimiter.description: Magic link emails per address: 2 per 30 minutes

passkeyChallengeLimiter.name: passkeyChallenge
passkeyChallengeLimiter.description: Passkey challenges per IP: 30 per hour, then blocked for 5 minutes

clientMetadataFetchLimiter.name: clientMetadataFetch
clientMetadataFetchLimiter.description: Client metadata fetches per IP: 60 per minute, then blocked for 1 minute

serviceBurstLimiter.name: serviceBurst
serviceBurstLimiter.description: Requests per actor with an API key or access token: 30 per second

mcpRequestLimiter.name: mcpRequest
mcpRequestLimiter.description: MCP requests per actor: 30 per second

syncReadLimiter.name: syncRead
syncReadLimiter.description: Sync reads per user: 5000 per hour, then blocked for 5 minutes

streamConnectLimiter.name: streamConnect
streamConnectLimiter.description: Live update stream connections per user: 240 per hour, then blocked for 5 minutes

yjsHttpLimiter.name: yjsHttp
yjsHttpLimiter.description: Yjs pulls and pushes per user: 7200 per hour, then blocked for 1 minute

pointsLimiter.name: points
pointsLimiter.description: API points per actor in a tenant: 1 per request, 1 per item on bulk routes, up to the tenant hourly budget

tokenLimiter.name: token
tokenLimiter.description: Failed link, callback and passkey sign-ins per IP: 10 per hour, then blocked for 30 minutes

insertEntityLock.name: insertEntityLock
insertEntityLock.description: Creates per tenant: 1 at a time

productCache.description: Entity-keyed detail cache with per-request read authorization

tags.name: cella
tags.description: Core modules provided by cella.

tags.name: app
tags.description: Application-specific modules.

tags.name: data
tags.description: Complete data schemas

tags.name: base
tags.description: Schemas with base fields only

tags.name: errors
tags.description: Error schemas

tags.name: channel
tags.description: Operations on channel entities (entities that have memberships, e.g. organizations, projects).

tags.name: product
tags.description: Operations on product entities (content entities without membership, e.g. tasks, pages, attachments).

tags.name: internal
tags.description: Operations hidden from the public API reference.

tags.name: activities
tags.description:
Audit log entries tracking create, update, and delete operations across all resources, written
    by the CDC worker. Activities provide an audit trail and can be extended for webhook delivery.

tags.name: attachments
tags.description:
Endpoints for managing file based attachments (such as images, PDFs, and documents) linked to
    entities such as organizations or users. Files are uploaded directly by the client, while the API handles
    metadata registration, linking, access, and preview utilities. The description is edited collaboratively
    and is a notification source for mentions.

tags.name: auth
tags.description:
Endpoints for authentication, supporting multiple sign-in methods including OAuth
    (Google, Microsoft, GitHub), institutional SSO through a federation (SURFconext) and passkeys (WebAuthn). They
    cover sign-up, sign-in, email verification, account linking, and impersonation for system admins.

tags.name: entities
tags.description:
Endpoints that operate across multiple entity types, such as users and organizations.
    Entities are identifiable domain objects that may be contextual, hierarchical (with parent/child
    relations), or actor-like. These routes provide shared logic across modules, including slug validation
    and entity visibility.

tags.name: mcp
tags.description:
Endpoints exposing the AI capability layer, which is a server-side MCP tool registry surfaced to
    external clients through a Model Context Protocol (MCP) endpoint. It ships no LLM transport or agent of its
    own; apps build AI features and agent products (such as chat) on top, reusing the same MCP tool registry.

tags.name: me
tags.description:
Endpoints scoped to the current user, meaning the user associated with the active session making
    the request. Unlike the users endpoints, which may operate on any user in the system, me endpoints act
    exclusively on the current user and follow a different authorization flow.

tags.name: oauth-server
tags.description:
The authorization server: node-oidc-provider on the app origin under /oauth, issuing the access
    tokens the API and the MCP endpoint accept. Runs as its own process (MODE=oauth) or folded into the API under
    singleVM; the store it writes is swept hourly by the jobs worker.

tags.name: memberships
tags.description:
Endpoints for managing memberships, which represent one-to-one relationships between a
    user and a contextual entity such as an organization. Each membership includes role information and
    status flags such as archived or muted. Memberships can also reference parent entities to easily have a
    hierarchical context available.

tags.name: metrics
tags.description: Endpoints for retrieving high-level counts for entities such as users and organizations.

tags.name: notifications
tags.description:
Per-recipient inbox for mentions and addressed activity, plus the daily/weekly
    email digest. Product modules opt in by declaring a notifications source on their own
    defineBackendModule call (who counts as a recipient is the only app-specific part); with no
    source declared the whole module is dormant. Rows are partitioned by createdAt so retention is
    automatic, and excluded from CDC because they are per-user state rather than synced content.

tags.name: organizations
tags.description:
Endpoints for managing organizations, which are core channel entities and the highest ancestor
    in the entity hierarchy. Organizations define access boundaries and are typically the primary scope for
    permissions and resource management.

tags.name: push
tags.description:
Web Push delivery for the notification inbox: per-device subscriptions, VAPID key
    exposure and the sender that turns fresh notification rows into pushes for offline
    subscribers. Dormant unless has.push is on AND the deployment carries VAPID keys.

tags.name: requests
tags.description:
Endpoints for handling incoming requests such as contact form submissions, newsletter signups,
    and waitlist entries.

tags.name: seen
tags.description: Endpoints for tracking entity view counts and marking entities as seen by the current user.

tags.name: service-accounts
tags.description:
Machine actors and their API keys. A service account is the actor an API key runs as: bound to
    the organization at a role, disabled rather than deleted, named in provenance like a user. Keys are opaque secrets
    shown once; a key may narrow what its account can do through scopes, never widen it.

tags.name: system
tags.description:
System level endpoints for administrative actions and platform wide functionality, such as user
    invitations, file uploads, and webhook handling.

tags.name: tenants
tags.description:
Endpoints for managing tenants, which are top-level isolation boundaries used by Row-Level
    Security (RLS) to partition data. Only system administrators can manage tenants.

tags.name: connections
tags.description:
Connections: the institutions a tenant trusts to assert its members' identities through an SSO
    federation (SURFconext first). System admins create them per tenant; a connection's id is the public entry key of
    the tenant's SSO sign-in, and its domains decide which asserted institution the sign-in accepts.

tags.name: users
tags.description:
Endpoints for managing users at the system level. Unlike channel entities such as
    organizations, a user is a global entity that is not scoped to a specific context. These endpoints are
    intended for administrative operations on any user in the system.

tags.name: yjs
tags.description:
Endpoints for Yjs collaborative editing support: a short-lived token per entity for the Yjs relay
    worker, and pull and push routes that sync a document through the API while the relay is out of reach. The relay's
    materialize route, which writes a compacted collaborative document to its entity, is served on the internal
    listener only.

cookieAuth.name: cella-development-session-v3
cookieAuth.description: Authentication cookie. Copy cookie from your network tab and paste it here. If you don't have it, you need to sign in or sign up first.

apiKey.description: Secret API key of a service account (`<app>_sk_live_…`), as `Authorization: Bearer` or `x-api-key`. Only routes that also accept it list it here.

oauth2.description: Access token from the authorization server, as `Authorization: Bearer`. Users consent through the authorization code flow (PKCE); service accounts use client credentials with a secret key as the client secret.

NotFoundError.description: Not found: resource does not exist.

UserMinimalBase.description: The smallest user shape: id, name, slug and avatar. Embedded wherever a row names a user, such as `createdBy` and `updatedBy`.

UserBase.description: The user fields shown to other users: name, slug, profile images, description and email. User lookups and member lists return it with the last-seen time added; member lists add the membership too.

ChannelBase.description: The fields every channel entity shares, such as organization; a channel owns memberships and roles. Used where a response names a channel without its details, such as the channel an invitation is for.

ProductBase.description: The fields every product entity shares, such as attachment: user-facing content that inherits access from its channel and syncs to clients. No endpoint returns it on its own; every product response starts with these fields.

example.name: Capitulus vesco cursim alter.
example.description: Veritas itaque basium a. Sufficio ter nostrum cilicium tersus ara. Earum ascit trans somniculosus.

MembershipBase.description: A user's membership in a channel without its audit fields: the role it grants, plus the member's own archive, mute and menu order. Returned for the signed-in user's own memberships, and as `included.membership` on a channel they belong to.

fieldTimestamps.description: Per-field HLC timestamps for scalar fields being changed

replayed.description: Set on a paused offline mutation being replayed: its field timestamps then arbitrate as intent time

StxBase.description: The sync envelope on every product write: a mutation ID, a source ID and per-field timestamps. Clients send it with each create and update; the server merges concurrent edits by its timestamps, and a client recognizes its own writes coming back by the source ID.

kind.description: Discriminant for the notification: product-entity sync vs membership change

action.description: Change kind; moveOut = the row left this path (reparent) and is no longer readable there

channelType.description: Channel entity type for membership events (e.g. organization, project)

path.description: Materialized id-path of the affected rows (root-first ancestor ids); moveOut carries the OLD path

seq.description: Org-sequence position (one order per organization, shared across product entity types)

channelId.description: Channel entity ID for grouping (e.g. projectId for tasks in unseen counts)

batchUntilSeq.description: Last sequence position for a batched notification: client should fetch range

count.description: Authoritative row count for batches: sequence ranges of different paths may interleave

spreadWindow.description: Server-suggested spread window (ms) for the lazy delta fetch; scales with channel audience and load, and the client clamps it between its priority tier bounds

embeddedProduct.description: Product type whose change triggered the propagation (e.g. label)

hostProduct.description: Host product type whose cache should be patched (e.g. task)

hostColumn.description: Column on the host product that embeds the changed product (e.g. labels)

update.description: Host product IDs that need cache refresh

remove.description: Host product IDs that need the embedded reference removed

propagation.description: Embedded-product propagation hint for cross-product cache invalidation

StreamNotification.description: A live notification that a product entity or a membership changed, naming the entity, its path and sequence range rather than the row. It arrives as a `change` event on `/entities/app/stream`; the client then fetches the changed rows through the regular API.

BadRequestError.description: The request is malformed or fails validation (400). `type` names the problem, such as `invalid_request`.

ApiError.description: The body of every error response. `type` is a stable code to branch on, `message` is readable text, and `requestId` identifies the request in the server logs.

UnauthorizedError.description: The request carries no valid session, API key or access token, or it expired (401). Sign in again, or send a valid key or token.

ForbiddenError.description: The caller is known but may not do this (403): their role denies the action, a recent step-up is required, or the action is refused while impersonating. `type` names the reason, such as `step_up_required`.

NotFoundError.description: The resource does not exist, or the caller may not read it (404). Both get the same answer, so a response never confirms that an id exists.

ConflictError.description: The request conflicts with the current state (409), such as a link that belongs to another account (`user_mismatch`) or a create already in progress. Reload the current state before retrying.

TooManyRequestsError.description: A rate limit refused the request (429). The `Retry-After` header says when to try again; an operation's rate limiters show what is counted.

status.description: Only `active` signs in; `pending` means the institution has not activated the app yet

SsoEntry.description: The sign-in entry of one institution at one organization: the federation it goes through, the institution, the organization, and whether it is active. Public by the connection's id, which is the link an institution shares.

isSystemAdmin.description: Whether the user holds the system admin role and the request comes from an allowed IP address.

Me.description: The signed-in user, with whether they have system admin access on this request. A client reads it to learn who is signed in.

User.description: A full user account: profile, preferences such as language and newsletter, the MFA setting and activity timestamps. Returned to the user themselves and to system admins; other users see the `UserBase` fields.

isNewDevice.description: The browser was first seen recently and is not the first one known.

MeAuthData.description: How the signed-in user signs in: connected OAuth providers, passkeys, whether TOTP is set up, and their live sessions. The account page lists it, where sessions can be ended and sign-in methods changed.

InactiveMembership.description: An invitation to join a channel that is not accepted yet: the invited email, the role and who invited. It becomes a membership once accepted; the signed-in user's invitations list it with the channel it is for.

publicBucket.description: Whether the upload is stored public-read in the public bucket; the template decides.

UploadToken.description: Permission to upload files with one upload template, signed for the upload service, with the storage prefix the files land under. A client requests one before uploading; the template decides whether files are stored public or private.

ConnectedApp.description: An app the signed-in user consented to: its OAuth client, the scopes it may use and when the consent expires. Listed under Connected apps in account settings, where the user can revoke it.

Request.description: A message from the public site: a contact message, a waitlist sign-up or a newsletter subscription. Anyone can send one, signed in or not; system admins list them.

example.message: Amitto sapiente antiquus temptatio verus mollitia.

apiPointsPerHour.description: Max API points per hour per user within this tenant (0 = no tenant limit; the global safety ceiling still applies)

allowUnregisteredClients.description: Whether members may consent to OAuth clients that have no registration (AI clients using a Client ID Metadata Document)

organization.description: The organization this tenant holds, or null if none

Tenant.description: The top-level isolation and billing boundary. Tenant and organization are 1:1: a tenant holds one organization, or none until that organization is created. System admins list and update tenants; a signed-in user can create one of their own.

idpEntityIds.description: The institution's IdP entity ids, passed as login_hint

logoUrl.description: The institution's logo, for the entry page

Connection.description: A tenant's trust in an external party that asserts user identities: an institution reached through an SSO federation, whose members sign in to the tenant's organization. Its id is the public key of the tenant's SSO entry page. System admins manage connections per tenant; `pending` until the institution activated the service at the federation.

ProtectedResourceMetadata.description: How an OAuth client gets an access token for this API or an MCP endpoint (RFC 9728): the authorization servers that issue tokens and the scopes accepted. A client finds it through the `WWW-Authenticate` header of a 401 response.

Organization.description: The channel entity every other channel nests under, owning memberships and roles. Tenant and organization are 1:1: an organization belongs to one tenant, and that tenant holds no other. Returned with `included` data: the signed-in user's membership, counts and member previews.

example.name: Spencer, Pouros and Bergnaum
example.welcomeText: Welcome to Spencer, Pouros and Bergnaum!

publicBucket.description: When true, the file is stored in the public bucket and served from the CDN without a presigned URL.

contentType.description: MIME type of the uploaded file (e.g. image/png).

convertedContentType.description: MIME type of the server-converted variant; null when none.

keys.description: Storage object keys per variant, keyed by variant name; only generated variants are present.

Attachment.description: A file in an organization: a product entity that syncs to clients and works offline. It holds the file metadata and storage keys, not the file itself; a client fetches the file through a signed URL.

ServiceAccount.description: An actor that is not a person, in one tenant: API keys run as it, and it holds role bindings like a member holds memberships. An organization admin creates one, for example with Create API key in organization settings.

ApiKey.description: A secret key a service account authenticates with, sent as `Authorization: Bearer` or `x-api-key`. Only its prefix and last four characters are returned after creation; it can expire and be revoked.

get.description: Returns auth health status including whether the client IP is rate-limited for email enumeration protection.

post.description: Tells whether this browser has signed in to the account with this email address before, by its device cookie. Any other browser gets `recognized: false`, whether or not the address has an account.

200.description: Whether this browser is recognized for the address

get.description: Opens an emailed link of a link-carried token type: a magic link or a provider address verification signs in, a step-up link proves presence on this browser's session, an invitation hands the app a single-use token session in a cookie. Redirects to the app.
Get basic token data from single-use token session, It returns basic data if the session is still valid.

post.summary: Accept invitation token as current user
post.description: Accepts the membership invitation held in the single-use token session as the signed-in user, also when it was sent to a different email address. Only an invitation not yet bound to another user can be accepted this way.
Allows a system admin to impersonate a specific user by ID, returning a temporary impersonation session.
Ends impersonation by clearing the current impersonation session and restoring the admin context.
Re-sends a pending invitation, named by the id of one of its tokens, to the address it went to. The fresh link replaces the older ones. Answers 204 whether or not an email went out.

204.description: Invitation email sent when the invitation is pending

post.description: Signs out the current user: the session is revoked (its row stays for the sessions list) and the cookie is cleared.
Sends a magic link sign-in email to the specified address. Always returns 204 to prevent email enumeration.

204.description: Magic link email sent (or silently ignored if email not found)

get.description: For a magic link opened in a browser that did not request it: the address it signs in, so the holder can recognize the account before confirming.

200.description: The full address the held link signs in, as the confirm page shows it

post.description: Signs in with the magic link this browser holds, confirmed from the app page. A form post from the app origin; redirects like opening the link.

302.description: Signed in, redirect to the app

post.description: Generates a new TOTP key for current user and returns a provisioning URI and Base32 manual key.
Confirms TOTP setup by verifying a code from the authenticator app for the first time. On success, TOTP is registered for current user.

delete.description: Delete TOTP credential for current user.

post.description: Validates the TOTP code and completes TOTP based authentication.
Register a passkey for passwordless authentication by verifying a signed challenge and linking it to the current user. Multiple passkeys can be created for different devices/browsers.

delete.description: Delete a passkey by id from the current user.

post.description: Initiates the passkey registration or authentication flow by generating a device bound challenge.
Validates the signed challenge and completes passkey based authentication.

Pins this browser's next provider sign-in with `type=connect` to the current user, for ten minutes and once: the provider's callback connects the provider account to the user that started it. Call it right before sending the browser to the provider.

get.description: Starts OAuth authentication with GitHub. Can be used for account connection, email verification, invitation process, defaults to authentication.
Starts OAuth authentication with Google. Can be used for account connection, email verification, invitation process, defaults to authentication.
Starts OAuth authentication with Microsoft. Can be used for account connection, email verification, invitation process, defaults to authentication.
Handles GitHub OAuth callback, retrieves user identity, and establishes a session or links account.
Handles Google OAuth callback, retrieves user identity, and establishes a session or links account.
Handles Microsoft OAuth callback, retrieves user identity, and establishes a session or links account.
What the entry page of an institution's sign-in shows: the organization, the institution and whether sign-in is active. Public by the connection id, the link an institution shares with its members.

Sends the browser to the connection's federation, pinned to the institution's identity providers, so its own picker is skipped. `type=connect` links the institution account to the signed-in user instead; other types are refused.
Sends the browser to the federation without naming an institution: the federation's own picker lists the connected ones, and the callback finds the connection by the institution the sign-in asserts.

The redirect URI registered at every federation. Verifies the tokens, asserts the institution against the connection, signs the user in (creating the account and its membership on a first sign-in) or links the identity, and redirects to the frontend.
Whether this session stands stepped up for account-security actions, and what the user can offer to step up: a passkey or TOTP they hold, else an emailed confirmation link or a new sign-in.

steppedUp.description: The session proved its user presence recently enough for account-security actions.

methods.description: What the user can offer to step up; empty while impersonating.

post.summary: Step up with a second factor
post.description: Proves the user is present on this session with a passkey assertion (to a step-up passkey challenge) or a TOTP code of a factor they hold. Account-security actions then pass for ten minutes.
Issues a passkey challenge for a step-up of this session, bound to the current user, with the user's passkeys to offer. Only a step-up answers it.
For a user without a passkey or TOTP: emails a confirmation link that steps up this session when opened in this browser within ten minutes. The link signs nobody in.

Checks whether a given slug is available within a tenant for the specified entity type.
      Primarily used to prevent slug collisions before creating or updating an entity.

get.description: SSE stream for membership and entity notifications affecting the current user. Sends lightweight notifications.

post.description: Fetch missed entity and membership changes since last sync. Send cursor and declared views (prefix sets + org-sequence cursors) in the body.

cursor.description: Last activity cursor received by the client (LSN-based). Omit on first sync.

key.description: Client-chosen stable view key, echoed back verbatim to correlate responses

prefixes.description: Materialized id-path prefixes this view covers (root-first ids, slash-joined)

depth.description: View depth: subtree (default) covers rows at or below the prefix node; self covers only rows HOMED at the node (exact placement: a channel wall). Self views are answerable by direct home-scoped memberships.

cursor.description: Org-sequence position this view has fully ingested (0 = baseline not yet established)

views.description: Client-declared views: prefix set + entity types + org-sequence cursor per view

embeddedProduct.description: Product type whose change triggered the propagation (e.g. label)

hostProduct.description: Host product type whose cache should be patched (e.g. task)

hostColumn.description: Column on the host product that embeds the changed product (e.g. labels)

update.description: Host product IDs that need cache refresh

remove.description: Host product IDs that need the embedded reference removed

key.description: The client-supplied view key, echoed verbatim

frontiers.description: Per-entityType newest sequence position over the view prefixes (subtree: f:{type}; self: fs:{type})

counts.description: Per-entityType live row counts summed over the view prefixes (subtree: e:{type}; self: es:{type})

views.description: Per-view answers for client-declared views (same order as the request)

cursor.description: Last activity ID (use as offset for next request)

get.description: Returns the current user.

delete.description: Deletes the current user. This also removes the user's memberships (cascade) and sets references to the user to null where applicable.

put.description: Enable or disable multifactor authentication for the current user. Needs a session stepped up with a passkey or TOTP.

get.description: Returns authentication related data of current user, including sessions, passkeys, TOTP and the enabled sign-in providers.
Returns a list of pending memberships with entity data.

delete.description: Revokes sessions of the current user by id. The rows stay for the audit trail and the sessions list shows them as revoked for 30 days. Revoking the current session signs out.

rejectedIds.description: Identifiers of items that could not be processed

rejectionReasons.description: Map of reason code to rejected item IDs

delete.description: Removes the current user from an entity they are a member of.

get.description: Generates and returns an upload token for uploading files or images, scoped to the current user and organization. The upload template decides the bucket: avatars, covers and newsletter images are public, attachments private. Only a system admin gets a newsletter image token.

200.description: Upload token with a scope for a user or organization

get.description: Returns all memberships for the current user across all channel entities.
Lists the OAuth clients the user consented to (MCP clients, registered apps) with their scopes.

delete.description: Revokes a consent: the grant and every token issued under it are deleted.

rejectedIds.description: Identifiers of items that could not be processed

rejectionReasons.description: Map of reason code to rejected item IDs

get.description:
Returns basic count metrics for entity types such as users and organizations.
      This endpoint is public and uses a 1 minute in memory cache for performance.

Returns the current user notification inbox, newest first, with the unread count. Ambient posts are not included: those are covered by unseen counts. Rows older than the retention window are removed with their partition.

schema.description: createdAt of the last row of the previous page

parameters.description: createdAt of the last row of the previous page
parameters.name: before

post.description: Marks specific notifications read by id, everything sharing one context, or all unread notifications when the body is empty. Idempotent.

contextId.description: Mark everything sharing one context read

get.description: Email and digest preferences for the current user. In-app delivery is not opt-out.

patch.description: Partial update; unspecified keys keep their stored value.

get.description: Turns off one email category from a link in an email. The token identifies the user and the category, so unsubscribing from the digest leaves other email untouched. No auth.

get.summary: Get the Web Push application server key
get.description: Returns the VAPID public key `PushManager.subscribe()` needs, or null when this deployment has no push keys configured; the client then offers no push toggle.

post.description: Stores the browser push subscription for the current user. Upserts by endpoint, so re-subscribing after key rotation reclaims the row.

delete.description: Deletes the given endpoint for the current user; an endpoint owned by someone else is a no-op.

post.description: Submits a request: a contact form message, a newsletter signup or a waitlist entry. Every submission gets the same answer: an address that has an account gets an email pointing to sign-in, and a repeat of a waitlist or newsletter signup is dropped.

get.description: Returns a list of submitted requests across all types: contact form, newsletter, and waitlist.

rejectedIds.description: Identifiers of items that could not be processed

rejectionReasons.description: Map of reason code to rejected item IDs

get.description: Returns the number of unseen product entities per parent channel entity (e.g., project) and entity type for the current user. Computed within the rolling seen window so entities older than seen_by retention do not participate.

200.description: Unseen counts per parent channel entity per entity type

post.description: Invites one or more users to the system via email. Can be used to onboard system level users or admins.

rejectedIds.description: Identifiers of items that could not be processed

rejectionReasons.description: Map of reason code to rejected item IDs

get.description: Returns an Ed25519-signed token for collaboratively editing one product entity the caller may update. It names the entity, its tenant and organization, and expires after five minutes; the Yjs relay worker verifies it with the public key alone, without a backend callback, and closes the socket when it expires.

post.description: Returns what the caller's copy of one product entity's collaborative document lacks, for a client that cannot reach the Yjs relay: the document's generation, an update holding what the caller's state vector lacks, and the server's state vector. A document never opened is seeded from the stored description first, as the relay seeds it. The caller must be allowed to update the entity, as for a Yjs token. A POST, since a state vector can outgrow a URL. Costs no API points.

stateVector.description: The caller's state vector: the answer carries what it lacks

generation.description: The document's generation: another one than the caller holds means the server reseeded it

update.description: What the caller's state vector lacks, as one Yjs update

stateVector.description: The server's state vector, so the caller can post what the server lacks

post.description: Appends one Yjs update to a product entity's collaborative document, for a client that cannot reach the Yjs relay. The answer follows the commit, so a 200 means the server holds the update; the relay passes it to live sessions and folds it into the document. An update made in another generation than the document's answers 409 `sync_document_replaced` with the current one in `meta.generation`, and with null when the document has no row: pull, which seeds it, then post again. At most 512 KB of update per request, base64url-encoded. The caller must be allowed to update the entity, as for a Yjs token. Costs no API points.

generation.description: The generation the update was made in

update.description: One Yjs update of at most 512 KB

status.description: `appended` once the update is logged; `empty` when it carried nothing the document lacked
